newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. Treasuries ease in Tokyo but mood bullish.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries ease in Tokyo but mood bullish.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were slightly softer by Tokyo midday on Thursday, but remained underpinned by the overall bullish mood, traders said.
"Some correction after the recent bull-run may be desirable, but market participants do not see reasons to sell. Pessimistic views are absent," said a trader at a Japanese brokerage house.
The 6-5/8 percent 30-year bond stood at 103-27/32, yielding 6.34 percent, as of 0305 GMT.
The long bond ended up 26/32 at 103-30/32 on Wednesday in New York.
Traders said the market will be watching the first official estimate of U.S. gross domestic product (GDP) for the second quarter due at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT.
Economists forecast on average growth of 1.9 percent, compared with 5.9 percent growth in the previous quarter.
"Today's GDP is old data, so it is unlikely to move the market much. A slowdown after hefty growth in the first quarter has already been factored in," said a trader at a U.S. brokerage house.
"People are more interested in Friday's July non-farm payrolls data," he added.
While operators agreed that the downside risk was limited for now, some said the market may need to be cautious about the recent uptick in commodity prices.

"Commodity prices overall have been showing a recovery from lows. This may not necessarily be indicative of higher inflation in the future, but we may still need to be vigilant," said the Japanese brokerage house trader.
The September T-bond futures contract stood at 116-14/32, up from 116-12/32 at the previous close. The contract moved in a range of 116-11 and 116-17.
